models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Pattern is very light and glassy - 2-5 kt, seas under 1 ft - but the trip dates themselves are still out of reach.
briefing.synopsis: No organised gradient over the Aeolians: ECMWF IFS and AIFS (both 30 Sep 00Z), with ICON-2i (29 Sep 12Z), show a slack pressure field with winds of roughly 2-5 kt at all six islands and total seas of 0.1-0.3 ft on MFWAM (29 Sep 12Z) and ECMWF WAM (30 Sep 00Z). What wind there is looks like a diurnal land/sea breeze cycle - SE to E overnight at Portorosa and NE at the islands, backing to NW-N by midday and early evening, peaking around 5-7 kt at Panarea and Stromboli at 18:00 on 1 Oct. If this pattern held into the trip it would mean motoring more than sailing, flat water and no anchorage that is pressed by wind or swell. That is a big if: the forecast only reaches 6 Oct, so the back half of the itinerary has no data at all.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For the night of 3 Oct at Portorosa, the payload recommends Portorosa Marina - an enclosed basin with all-round shelter, and the only option scored there. Conditions at that hour are given as 2 kt from the SE, gusting 6.4 kt, with 0.1 ft swell from the NW, so the berth choice does not matter in any practical sense. Nothing in the current data would push the fleet to move; a change would take a genuine gradient wind appearing in later runs, which is exactly what we will be watching for.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: This is a pre-trip outlook, not a departure briefing - the first leg, Portorosa to Lipari, is on 4 Oct. For that day the recommended departure is 06:00, with 5.6 kt SSE, gusts 11.5 kt and 0.1 ft seas, giving a dead run at 176 TWA; wind falls to 1.5-4 kt and swings E then N through the afternoon. Expect to confirm or discard all of that with the runs over the next two days.

passage_notes.note: Scored go. Best window 06:00-09:00: 5.6 kt SSE, gusts 11.5 kt, 0.1 ft seas, a run. After 10:00 wind drops to 1.5-4 kt and backs E then N - motoring.
Scored go, 2-4.7 kt W to NW all day, 0.1 ft seas. Short hop, no timing pressure in this data; likely a motor.
Scored go, 2.1-5.3 kt WNW-NW, 0.1 ft seas. Best breeze late (5.3 kt at 14:00) but that arrives 18:00 - weigh against an early start.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (6 Oct, 11 nm, 219°T)
passage_notes.note: Scored go, a flat 3 kt N all day, seas 0.2-0.4 ft, broad reach. Last leg with any forecast coverage.

passage_notes.leg: Panarea → Filicudi, Filicudi → Salina and beyond
passage_notes.note: No forecast - outside the 6 Oct horizon. These only appear in the rehearsal run against this week's live weather, which is not a forecast for your dates.

cautions: Trip dates are not yet covered: the data reaches 2026-10-06 only, and ICON-2i runs just 60-72 h ahead, so it drops out entirely for the later legs.
Direction, not strength, is the unreliable part. Forecast stability at 72-120 h lead shows a mean direction shift of 67 degrees against a mean wind shift of only 0.8 kt.

Where models disagree by more than 6 kt the payload flags it: Portorosa 30 Sep 12Z spans 0.6-7.2 kt, Portorosa 1 Oct 00Z spans 0.3-8.2 kt, Filicudi 1 Oct 12Z spans 2.2-8.9 kt. Treat the means at those hours as indicative only.

Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli scores only 'workable' and is marked no-anchoring - it is open from every direction, so its shelter depends entirely on the calm holding. That is the one berth in the itinerary with no fallback.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree closely on a light, slack pattern through 6 Oct, but the departure is 3 days out and everything from 7 Oct onward has no model data at all.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
